data.description:
## Description
**What**: Build plugins/dso/hooks/lib/static-defense-lib.sh providing four reusable primitives: (1) staged-.sh enumeration over diff-filter A/C/M/R/T, (2) count-based shrink-only baseline load and diff (reject when post-commit count exceeds recorded baseline; reject removing a baseline entry without removing its source violation), (3) suppression-annotation parsing for `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` and `# bash4-only:` requiring a non-empty non-whitespace token, and (4) diagnostic formatting emitting offending line, remediation string, and originating-ticket citation. The library resolves its own paths via BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f, never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
**Why**: All four hooks are thin wrappers over this library; proving enumeration completeness (sc-7) and bash-3.2 self-compatibility (sc-8) here once avoids divergence and re-implementation across hooks.
**Scope**:
- IN: the shared library file; its enumeration, baseline, suppression, and diagnostic functions; a fixture suite exercising those functions; a bash-3.2-constrained test for the library.
- OUT: the four concrete detection hooks; .pre-commit-config.yaml registration; the known-antipatterns.yaml registry.

## Done Definitions

- static-defense-lib.sh enumerates staged .sh files for git diff-filter classes added, copied, modified, and renamed/mode-changed, and a renamed file carrying a violation appears in the enumerated set ← Satisfies: sc-7
- static-defense-lib.sh loads a per-hook count-based baseline and reports a violation only when the staged-content count exceeds the recorded baseline; a commit that removes a baseline entry while its source violation remains is reported as a rejected grow operation ← Satisfies: sc-2
- static-defense-lib.sh parses `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` and `# bash4-only:` annotations and treats an empty or whitespace-only justification token as a rejected suppression ← Satisfies: sc-5
- static-defense-lib.sh formats a per-file diagnostic that contains the offending line text, the remediation string, and the originating-ticket citation ← Satisfies: sc-3
- static-defense-lib.sh executes under a bash-3.2-constrained interpreter with no declare -A or nameref usage, verified by a bash-3.2 test that passes ← Satisfies: sc-8
- unit tests (fixture-based) are written and passing for all new enumeration, baseline, suppression, and diagnostic logic in static-defense-lib.sh ← Satisfies: sc-6

## Considerations

- [Hermeticity] The library MUST resolve its own path and baseline locations via the BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f idiom used by check-tickets-boundary.sh, never via CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, so it works under the pre-commit framework symlinked temp-path chain and in CI where CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset.
- [Compatibility] static-defense-lib.sh must not itself ship the bash-4-only antipattern (declare -A, namerefs) that check-known-antipatterns.sh is meant to flag.
- [Build] static-defense-lib.sh and any new .sh fixtures/tests must have the executable bit set (CLAUDE.md always:chmod-x-new-sh).
- [Baseline-format] The library owns one consistent baseline format (count-based) to avoid integer-vs-file-keyed-map ambiguity across hooks.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a hook author, I want a shared static-defense-lib.sh providing bash-3.2-safe staged-file enumeration (A/C/M/R), baseline comparison, diagnostics, and suppression parsing, so the four defense hooks share one correct foundation
